usageNotes: Use this to format an unused block device with ext4 or xfs and mount it as a directory-backed storage under '/mnt/pve/NAME'. The target device must be completely unpartitioned and unused — Proxmox will refuse if the disk has any existing partition table or filesystem. The operation returns a task UPID; poll the task status to confirm completion before referencing the new storage.

examples.summary: Format /dev/sdb with ext4 and register it as a Proxmox directory storage named 'local-data'

tips: Use get_nodes_node_disks_list first to identify unused disks (those with no partition table reported).
Setting add_storage=true saves a separate step but requires the calling token/user to also hold 'Datastore.Allocate' on /storage, in addition to Sys.Modify on /.
xfs is preferred for large sequential workloads (e.g. backup targets, ISO stores); ext4 is the safe default for general use.
Once created, the directory storage appears in Datacenter > Storage and is immediately usable for VM disks, backups, and ISOs depending on content types configured afterward.
To undo, you must manually remove the storage from Proxmox config and unmount/wipe the device — there is no API delete counterpart for this specific create path.
